messages:
anya: Heads up — after rotating the envelope CMK for billing-prod the nightly decrypt in the rotator Lambda started failing :grimacing:
kevin: paste the error?
anya: 
```
KMS.DecryptAccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/rotator-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```
anya: It used to work before rotation, same role. We only swapped the key policy with our standard template.
sam: remember KMS evaluates the actual principal (the assumed-role ARN). If your key policy lists the role ARN but not the assumed-role pattern, requests can be denied.
anya: I pasted the policy we applied below — could be the problem:
```
{
  \"Version\": \"2012-10-17\",
  \"Statement\": [
    {
      \"Sid\": \"PermitRotator\",
      \"Effect\": \"Allow\",
      \"Principal\": {\"AWS\": \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rotator-role\"},
      \"Action\": [\"kms:Decrypt\", \"kms:GenerateDataKey\"],
      \"Resource\": \"*\"
    }
  ]
}
```
kevin: that principal is the static role ARN — KMS receives an sts assumed-role principal (arn:aws:sts::...:assumed-role/rotator-role/<session-name>). Fixes: allow the account root and use a Condition StringLike on aws:PrincipalArn, or set Principal to the account and use IAM policies for the role.
sam: example condition-based statement that matches assumed role sessions:
```
{
  \"Sid\": \"AllowAssumedRotator\",
  \"Effect\": \"Allow\",
  \"Principal\": {\"AWS\": \"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root\"},
  \"Action\": [\"kms:Decrypt\", \"kms:GenerateDataKey*\"],
  \"Resource\": \"*\",
  \"Condition\": {
    \"StringLike\": {\"aws:PrincipalArn\": \"arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/rotator-role/*\"}
  }
}
```
linda: also double-check for an explicit Deny coming from an org SCP, permissions boundary, or a key policy statement that denies based on aws:SourceVpc / aws:SourceIp. That can silently block lambdas behind NAT.
kms-audit-bot: cloudtrail: 2024-03-12T07:12:44Z KMS Decrypt AccessDenied principal=arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/rotator-role/rotation-2024-03-12 keyId=abcd-ef01-2345
anya: we also use a temporary grant token during rotation and the lambda passes GrantTokens on decrypt, but it still fails.
kevin: grants are tricky — ensure the grant actually exists (`aws kms list-grants --key-id <key>`) and that the grant principal matches the assumed-role arn. Grants are independent of key policy and contain their own constraints; if you pass a grant token, it must be valid and not expired.
sam: quick checklist to triage:
• confirm CloudTrail shows the exact principal (assumed-role vs role)
• update key policy to cover assumed-role patterns or allow account root + condition
• verify no SCP/permissions boundary denies
• run `aws kms list-grants` and confirm grant token/principal
• test `aws sts get-caller-identity` from the failing execution environment to mirror principal
• try a minimal reproduce: assume the role from your workstation and call `kms:Decrypt` against the new key

anya: thanks — I'll try changing the key policy to the StringLike principal-arn condition and re-run rotation in canary. Will report back if it still errors.
kevin: ping me if you want me to run a repro assume-role + decrypt in my account. Happy to help. :+1:
